content:
Hi Mara — Professor Alvarez wants to schedule next week's CSE455 staff meeting (30 min, all TAs). Which of these work for you? Please reply with all that fit:

- Monday 10:00–10:30
- Monday 14:00–14:30
- Tuesday 11:00–11:30
- Tuesday 15:00–15:30
- Wednesday 10:00–10:30
- Wednesday 13:00–13:30

Thanks!

Hi Sarah — Professor Alvarez wants to schedule next week's CSE455 staff meeting (30 min, all TAs). Which of these work for you? Please reply with all that fit:

- Monday 10:00–10:30
- Monday 14:00–14:30
- Tuesday 11:00–11:30
- Tuesday 15:00–15:30
- Wednesday 10:00–10:30
- Wednesday 13:00–13:30

Thanks!

Hi John — Professor Alvarez wants to schedule next week's CSE455 staff meeting (30 min, all TAs). Which of these work for you? Please reply with all that fit:

- Monday 10:00–10:30
- Monday 14:00–14:30
- Tuesday 11:00–11:30
- Tuesday 15:00–15:30
- Wednesday 10:00–10:30
- Wednesday 13:00–13:30

Thanks!

Hi Professor Alvarez — none of those windows work cleanly for me next week. If possible, could we push the CSE455 staff meeting to the following week instead? If it needs to stay next week, send a couple of other options and I’ll take another look.

These work for Sarah:

- Tuesday 11:00-11:30
- Tuesday 15:00-15:30
- Wednesday 10:00-10:30
- Wednesday 13:00-13:30

These work for John:

- Monday 10:00-10:30
- Monday 14:00-14:30
- Tuesday 15:00-15:30
- Wednesday 10:00-10:30
- Wednesday 13:00-13:30

Tuesday 11:00-11:30 does not fit.

Thanks Mara — noted that none of those work for you. I'm collecting responses from Sarah and John too, then I'll find the best fit. If nothing lines up cleanly next week, I'll look at the following week as you suggested. Will circle back shortly.
Thanks, Professor Alvarez — that sounds good. I appreciate it.

I've acknowledged Mara. Now I'm waiting on Sarah and John before I can settle the meeting time. Mara has ruled out all six slots and prefers the following week, so a next-week booking would need to work around her — I'll see what the other two say and then find the best path.

I'll follow up here once Sarah and John respond.

Note: I did not schedule a reminder in this turn, so this will not trigger automatically.

Sarah gave me four workable slots. Still waiting on John. I'll note Sarah's availability and hold until John responds to find the common slot.

Sarah's options: Tue 11:00, Tue 15:00, Wed 10:00, Wed 13:00. Once John replies, I'll intersect all three. Note: Mara ruled out everything, so unless John's answer changes things, a next-week slot won't include Mara — I may need to either proceed without Mara or move to the following week per her request.

I'll wait for John before making that call and will follow up here.
Understood. Sarah is available for Tue 11:00, Tue 15:00, Wed 10:00, and Wed 13:00, and I’ll hold for your follow-up once John responds.

All three have responded. Let me find the common slot.

- **Mara:** none of the six work
- **Sarah:** Tue 11:00, Tue 15:00, Wed 10:00, Wed 13:00
- **John:** Mon 10:00, Mon 14:00, Tue 15:00, Wed 10:00, Wed 13:00

Sarah ∩ John: **Tue 15:00–15:30, Wed 10:00–10:30, Wed 13:00–13:30**. But Mara can make none of these.

Since there's no slot that works for all three next week, and Mara explicitly asked to push to the following week, the cleanest path is to move the whole meeting to the following week so everyone can attend. However, the calendar I manage only covers next week, and the professor's original request was to set it up for next week.

This is a genuine decision point. Rather than book a meeting that excludes a TA or unilaterally push to a week I have no calendar for, I'll present the situation to the professor.

Here's where things landed:

**No single slot works for all three TAs next week.**
- **Mara:** none of the six offered slots work; she asked to move it to the *following* week.
- **Sarah & John** overlap on: **Tue 15:00–15:30, Wed 10:00–10:30, Wed 13:00–13:30** (all fine on your calendar).

So your options:

1. **Book next week without Mara** — e.g. Wed 10:00–10:30 (Sarah + John + you). I'd then loop Mara in separately.
2. **Move the whole meeting to the following week** so all three can attend, as Mara requested. (Note: my calendar only covers next week, so I'd need slots/confirmation for that week.)

Which would you like? If you want option 1, tell me which of the three slots; if option 2, I'll poll everyone for the following week.

Thanks Mara! Nothing's locked in yet — I'm confirming the final plan with Professor Alvarez (either a next-week slot or moving to the following week so you can join). I'll send you the confirmed time as soon as it's set.

From John’s side: if you want everyone present, moving the staff meeting to the following week seems like the best option since no next-week slot works for all three and Mara asked for that.

If you decide to meet next week without Mara, John can still do:
- Tuesday 15:00-15:30
- Wednesday 10:00-10:30
- Wednesday 13:00-13:30
Thanks, Professor Alvarez — I appreciate the update. Please keep me posted once the time is confirmed.

Nothing new to act on — Mara's message was just a thank-you, and I've already acknowledged it. The situation is unchanged: no meeting is booked, and I'm waiting on Professor Alvarez to choose between booking a next-week slot (without Mara) or moving to the following week so all three TAs can attend.

No action needed until the professor decides.

Sarah is just reconfirming her availability and holding — nothing new to decide. All three TAs have already responded, so John's input is in. No new action is required.

The situation remains: no common slot for all three next week, and I'm waiting on Professor Alvarez to choose between booking without Mara or moving to the following week.
Understood. Sarah’s availability is unchanged, and we’ll wait for Professor Alvarez’s decision on whether to book without Mara or move the meeting to the following week.

John is reinforcing the same picture: no next-week slot works for all three, and he recommends moving to the following week to include everyone. This is helpful input but doesn't change that the decision still belongs to Professor Alvarez.

I've already presented the two options to the professor and I'm waiting on his call. John's message adds a clear consensus signal (Mara wants it moved, John agrees moving is best, Sarah is flexible), which I'll surface to the professor so he has the full picture.

Quick update before you decide: **John also recommends moving to the following week** so everyone can attend, echoing Mara. Sarah remains flexible either way.

So the consensus among the TAs leans toward **option 2 (move to the following week)**:
- **Mara:** can't do any next-week slot; asked to move it.
- **John:** recommends moving; but if you go next week without her, he can do Tue 15:00, Wed 10:00, or Wed 13:00.
- **Sarah:** flexible — Tue 11:00, Tue 15:00, Wed 10:00, Wed 13:00.

Your call:
1. **Move to the following week** — I'll poll all three for slots that week and book once they align.
2. **Next week without Mara** — pick Wed 10:00–10:30 or Wed 13:00–13:30 (both work for Sarah + John), and I'll loop Mara in separately.

Which do you prefer?

Mara's message is just another acknowledgment — she's thanking me for the update and asking to be kept posted. Nothing to book, and the professor still hasn't chosen between the two options. No new decision or action is warranted.

I've already told Mara I'll send her the confirmed time once it's set, so no further reply is needed here.

That matches John’s position. No change on his side: he supports moving the meeting to the following week so everyone can attend.

If you decide to keep it next week without Mara, John is still available Tuesday 15:00-15:30, Wednesday 10:00-10:30, and Wednesday 13:00-13:30. If you move it to the following week, send over candidate slots and I’ll confirm John’s availability there.

Sarah's message is another acknowledgment reconfirming unchanged availability and waiting for the professor's decision. No new information and nothing to act on — the meeting still can't be booked until Professor Alvarez chooses between the two options.

No reply needed.

John is reiterating his position again — no new information. All three TAs have now restated the same thing multiple times: no next-week slot works for all three, and the consensus leans toward moving to the following week.

The decision genuinely rests with Professor Alvarez, and I've already presented both options clearly. There's nothing new to act on, and no further loop of acknowledgments with the TAs adds value. I'll stay put and wait for the professor's decision.
No further change from John’s side. I’ll wait for your decision on whether to move the staff meeting to the following week or keep a next-week slot without Mara.

John's message is another restatement with no new information — he's just confirming he'll wait for the decision. The TAs have now cycled through several rounds of acknowledgments, all reinforcing the same picture.

Nothing has changed: no meeting can be booked until Professor Alvarez decides between moving to the following week or booking next week without Mara. There's no new action to take, and replying again would only add noise to the loop.
